code.note: The demo needs the GNU Scientific Library (GSL): the Makefile points at /usr/local by default (gsllib). Build the demo from the archive's own Makefile, run the test binary with no arguments (the default script TEST_default.sh does this), and read table row x = 5.00e+00 in the output. The claim is the f_comp value in that row, which the shipped output prints as 1.29653819e+00. The elapsed-time lines are machine-dependent and are not claimed.

field: numerics (Laplace transform inversion by algorithmic differentiation)

claim.location: Shipped output of the authors' default demo run, scripts/output_demo2_default_EXAMPLE/output_demo2.txt, the TABLE row for x = 5.00e+00: f_comp = 1.29653819e+00 (with Used tolerance 0.001000, abscissa of convergence 1.000000, maximum coefficients 2000, and Nopt = Ncal = 18).

reference.sha256: not computed by scout; the rerun should hash the shipped file and record it

claim.paper_value: 1.29653819 (f_comp at x = 5 in the shipped default demo output; the paper's own numbers are not read here)
claim.metric: f_comp returned by the RELIADIFF inversion at x = 5 for the demo's test function, compared as a number
claim.determinism: deterministic (fixed test function, fixed default tolerance and abscissa, no random input; the Nopt = 18 count is also fixed by those settings)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The printed value has 9 significant figures, so its rounding step is 1e-8 at this magnitude; a rerun that rounds the other way differs by one unit. 2e-8 allows two units and nothing larger. Not to be loosened after any run. A rerun whose GSL version changes the value beyond this should record the GSL version and be diagnosed, not re-tolerated.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 5 minutes to build; the default demo runs in about 7 ms of inversion time (the output's own elapsed-time line).
cost.data_size: None: the demo generates its own inputs.
cost.data_licence: No data. The archive licence is not stated; the rerun should record it.

why: The demo inverts a known Laplace transform with the package's algorithmic differentiation and prints the computed values; the value at x = 5 needs the full inversion to run, so it tests the code rather than a closed form, and the authors' own shipped output is the reference.
